metadata.note: Blue Ridge Railroad of South Carolina: one 44-mile line Belton - Anderson - Pendleton - Seneca - West Union - Walhalla, no branches. Belton - Anderson was never Blue Ridge property (it was the Greenville and Columbia's Anderson Branch, later C&G / R&D / Southern, used exclusively by the Blue Ridge Railway from 1901). The operator changed five times, so the line is drawn as ten features over four shared pieces of geometry (Belton - Anderson, Anderson - Pendleton, Pendleton - West Union, West Union - Walhalla), one per drawable span and operator (Rule 4), exactly as the research report's drawable: fields give them. Rule 4 company decisions: (a) 'Blue Ridge Railroad' (1852 company, incl. its 1894-1901 receivership) and 'Blue Ridge Railway' (1901) are treated as DIFFERENT companies with different colours: the Railway was a new corporation chartered by Southern nominees that bought the property at a foreclosure sale after seven years of receivership, with new ownership, and the two never ran trains in continuity of management. (b) 'Greenville and Columbia Railroad' and 'Columbia and Greenville Railroad' likewise are kept separate (the 1880 foreclosure reorganisation the report lists as an operator change); the existing columbia_upstate.geojson runs G&C straight through 1880 under multi-company strings and so supplies no colour for either. Nothing is drawn after 1927: the 1 Jul 1951 Carolina and Northwestern lease is freight-only by the Feb 1952 Official Guide (Rule 1). The never-completed Walhalla - Stumphouse Tunnel - Clayton - Knoxville extension carried no trains and is not drawn.
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt, C&NW table ~line 106210-106280; index legend 247302-247306)
https://www.branchline.uk (Fowler's South Carolina list, Blue Ridge Rly table 39 - mileposts only)

metadata.not_yet_sourced: (1) [OPEN] Blue Ridge Railway: Belton - Walhalla is drawn to 1927, the last confirmed year (Keowee Courier 'mid-day train', 1 Jun 1927; 1921 is the last fully explicit passenger mention). The real end lies in 1927-1951 and the secondary sources CONFLICT: the 1976 Anderson Blue Ridge passenger station marker / Random Connections blog say passenger service ended 'around 1945' (possibly the Main Street station only), while Wikipedia says 'by the latter part of 1951', citing Aug 1949 and Dec 1951 Official Guides not seen. The Feb 1952 Guide proves freight-only by 30 Sep 1951 only. A 1930s/1940s Official Guide or Southern system timetable with a Blue Ridge Railway table, or an Anderson Independent / Keowee Courier last-train story, would settle it. (2) [ANCHOR] Blue Ridge Railroad: Pendleton - West Union drawn for 1866 only; opening between Sept 1860 and Apr 1866 (ICC: completed 1861), and whether trains ran 1861-65, unproven. (3) [ANCHOR] Southern Railway: Belton - Anderson drawn for 1895 only, from a connection note; 1894-1901 likely. (4) Anderson - Pendleton and Belton - Anderson starts are the earliest confirmed year (1860), not openings (c.1857-59 and c.1853 claimed, unverified); 1861-65 on Anderson - Pendleton assumed continuous. (5) West Union - Walhalla 14 Nov 1877 is Wikipedia's date, not checked against a primary source; railga.com / carolana.com claim Walhalla in 1859 (refuted for 1860 by the Pendleton railhead notice). (6) Start of the G&C lease between Apr 1866 and Dec 1867, and whether it lapsed c.1869-71. (7) R&D lease date 1886 from the columbia_upstate layer / Wikipedia, not independently checked. (8) headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates from OCR'd tables throughout.

segments.note: Blue Ridge Railroad's own trains, connecting with the Greenville and Columbia at Anderson. Anderson Intelligencer 28 Aug 1860 (also Keowee Courier, Sept and 1 Dec 1860): 'CARS on the Blue Ridge Railroad leave Pendleton on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays ... Leave Anderson ... immediately after the cars arrive from Belton' - thrice weekly each way, Pendleton the railhead. Anderson Intelligencer 12 Apr 1866: trains leave Anderson for Pendleton and Walhalla Wednesdays and Saturdays (W. H. D. Gaillard, Superintendent B.R.R.R.). START 1860 is the EARLIEST CONFIRMED year, not the opening: rails reportedly reached Pendleton by Jan 1857 (search snippet, unverified) and carolana.com says 1859 - do not move the start without a dated notice. 1861-1865 are drawn on the assumption of continuity; no wartime timetable was found, so a strict reading is 1860 and 1866 anchors only. Ends 1866: the Greenville and Columbia was working the road under lease by Dec 1867 (see that feature). carolana.com's claim that the G&C leased the road in 1859 conflicts with the 1866 Blue Ridge superintendent's notice; recorded, not resolved. headway_min 3360 = thrice weekly (1860); twice weekly by 1866.
sources: Segment-level: Anderson Intelligencer 1860-08-28 p4 and 1866-04-12 p3, Keowee Courier 1860-12-01 p3 (Chronicling America) name the service and its frequency; 1861-1865 unproven.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] Single proven year of company operation on this piece. Anderson Intelligencer 12 Apr 1866: 'Trains on the Blue Ridge Railroad will leave Anderson for Pendleton and Walhalla, on Wednesdays and Saturdays' (W. H. D. Gaillard, Superintendent). Service certainly ran wider than 1866 - the ICC valuation says the road was 'completed in 1861' and the railhead was still Pendleton in Sept 1860 - but no other year of passenger service on this piece is confirmed, so do not widen the anchor without a dated timetable. The 'Walhalla' of the 1866 notice is almost certainly the West Union depot: rails reached Walhalla itself only in Nov 1877. Seneca did not yet exist (the Air Line came through in 1873). headway_min 5040 = twice weekly.

segments.note: The Greenville and Columbia Railroad worked the Blue Ridge Railroad under lease. Daily Phoenix 5 Dec 1867, G&C 'Change of Schedule': 'Trains on the Blue Ridge Railroad will also run daily, Sundays excepted ... Leave Anderson 5.20 p.m., Pendleton 6.20, Arrive at Walhalla 8.00' (James O. Meredith, G&C General Superintendent). G&C annual report, Daily Phoenix 17 Apr 1869: the Blue Ridge 'is still being worked by our Company' (termination expected but evidently not made). Anderson Intelligencer 11 Jan 1872: G&C through running Columbia - Belton - Anderson - Pendleton - Walhalla. Anderson Intelligencer 20 May 1880: G&C 'Anderson Branch & Blue Ridge R.R.' table, Belton - Anderson - Pendleton - Perryville - Seneca City - Walhalla. 1867, 1869, 1872 and 1880 are confirmed. Start 1867: the lease began after the Apr 1866 company-run notice and by Dec 1867. End 1880 is an era end, not a service end: the property was deeded to the G&C on 1 Jul 1880 and the Columbia and Greenville succeeded the G&C on 23 Nov 1880 (see that feature). West Union was the railhead to Nov 1877; the extension to Walhalla is its own feature. The 1868-1874 'Blue Ridge ring' bond scandal did not change who ran the trains. headway_min 1440 = one round trip daily except Sunday.
sources: Segment-level: Daily Phoenix 1867-12-05 p4 and 1869-04-17 p2, Anderson Intelligencer 1872-01-11 p2 and 1880-05-20 p4 (Chronicling America).

segments.note: The Columbia and Greenville Railroad (successor by foreclosure reorganisation to the Greenville and Columbia) took the G&C and the Blue Ridge property on 23 Nov 1880 and ran Belton - Anderson (its own) and Anderson - Walhalla (Blue Ridge RR). Anderson Intelligencer 1 Jun 1882: 'Columbia and Greenville Railroad. CHANGE OF SCHEDULE ... Passenger Trains over the Columbia and Greenville Road will be run daily, Sundays excepted', Anderson / Pendleton / Seneca City / Walhalla both ways. Anderson Intelligencer 30 Apr 1885: 'About five years ago the Blue Ridge Railroad belonged to the Greenville & Columbia'. 1882 is confirmed inside the era; both ends are corporate dates. End 1886: the C&G was leased to the Richmond and Danville in 1886 - date taken from the existing columbia_upstate layer / Wikipedia, not independently checked. The C&G resurveyed Walhalla - Clayton, Ga. in 1881-82 but never built it. headway_min 1440 = one round trip daily except Sunday (1882).
sources: Segment-level: Anderson Intelligencer 1882-06-01 p4 (Chronicling America) for service; ICC valuation for the 1880 transfer. The 1886 end (R&D lease) is not independently sourced.

segments.note: Richmond and Danville Railroad, lessee of the Columbia and Greenville, ran the line as part of its Columbia & Greenville Division. End 1894: from 1 Jan 1894 the Blue Ridge property (Anderson - Walhalla) was run by receivers and Belton - Anderson passed to the Southern - so the R&D's last full year was 1893; 1894 is drawn as the report's era-end year and overlaps the receiver's first year. headway_min 1440 is an estimate (the 1890 table's train count was not tallied).

segments.note: Blue Ridge Railroad in receivership (H. C. Beattie, Receiver; J. B. Anderson, Supt.) - a separate operation, NOT the Southern. Anderson Intelligencer 1 Jul 1896: 'BLUE RIDGE RAILROAD, H. C. BEATTIE, Receiver. Time Table In effect April 21, 1895. Between Anderson and Walhalla, Daily' - one round trip daily, 'Close connection with Southern Railway No. 11 at Seneca and No. 12 at Anderson'. The receiver's trains ran Anderson - Walhalla only; Belton - Anderson was the Southern's (see that feature). ICC: receivers from 1 Jan 1894; foreclosure sale 15 Jul 1901; the Blue Ridge Railway took over 28 Sep 1901. railga.com's 'Southern acquired the line in 1894' is wrong about who ran it. 1895-96 confirmed inside the era; both ends are corporate dates. Rule 4: same company and colour as the 1860-1866 Blue Ridge Railroad - the receiver ran the same corporation's property.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] Single proven year. The Blue Ridge receiver's table in effect 21 Apr 1895 (Anderson Intelligencer 1 Jul 1896) connects with 'Southern Railway ... No. 12 at Anderson'; the only Southern line into Anderson was this branch from Belton (the old G&C Anderson Branch, which the Southern took with the Columbia and Greenville in 1894), so Southern passenger trains ran it. Inferred from a connection note, not a Southern table - hence the anchor. Southern operation certainly ran wider (very likely 1894-1901, until the Blue Ridge Railway took exclusive use), but no other year is confirmed; do not widen without a Southern timetable of the period. headway_min 1440 is an estimate (at least train No. 12 daily).
sources: Segment-level: Anderson Intelligencer 1896-07-01 p4 (Chronicling America), connection note only.

segments.note: [OPEN] Blue Ridge Railway Company, chartered 28 Sep 1901 by Southern Railway nominees after the foreclosure sale; Southern-controlled but, per the ICC valuation, 'the carrier has always operated its own property' (some Southern equipment), so this is not drawn as Southern. It owned Anderson - Walhalla (34.277 mi) and had exclusive use of the Southern-owned Belton - Anderson (9.908 mi). Keowee Courier 7 Jan 1903: 'BLUE RIDGE RAILWAY CO. BETWEEN BELTON AND WALHALLA. Time Table No. 6 - In Effect Nov. 2, 1902', two trains each way. Keowee Courier 20 Nov 1918: Time Table No. 24, effective 21 Apr 1918, several trains each way (OCR too mangled to count). Keowee Courier 24 Aug 1921: excursionists 'can take regular Blue Ridge trains' (No. 2 Walhalla 7.10 a.m., Seneca 7.45, Anderson 9.00, Belton 9.30). Keowee Courier 1 Jun 1927: 'The schedule on the mid-day train of the Blue Ridge Railway has been changed' (train type not stated; 1921 is the last fully explicit passenger year). Anderson's Main Street passenger station opened 1915. Passenger service confirmed to 1927. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - the Keowee Courier's Chronicling America run stops in 1927, a source edge. Service ended somewhere in 1927-1951: the Anderson station marker says c.1945, Wikipedia says 'by the latter part of 1951' (citing the Aug 1949 and Dec 1951 Official Guides, not seen), and the Feb 1952 Official Guide shows the line freight-only under the Carolina and Northwestern, lessee from 1 Jul 1951. Do not extend without evidence. headway_min 720 = two each way (1902); more by 1918 - an estimate for the span.
sources: Segment-level: Keowee Courier 1903-01-07 p4, 1918-11-20 p3, 1921-08-24 p8 and 1927-06-01 p8 (Chronicling America); ICC valuation for the company and its operation. The end is OPEN.
